turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
I came in because... well, my mind just keeps going completely blank at the absolute worst times. I'll be out there at work, and I'll look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle... which, they actually gave us new paddles last month. They're supposed to be lighter, made of this weird aluminum stuff, but the handle gets freezing cold in the mornings. I tried wearing my wool gloves, the ones my sister knitted for me, but then I can't grip the radio right. She used this really scratchy purple yarn anyway, she always buys the cheap stuff from the craft store downtown. 

But... what was I saying? Right, the paddle. I'll just look at it, or the forms, and suddenly I cannot remember the steps I have done for years. Just gone. It’s like my brain just empties out. And then the traffic starts backing up, and people are honking, and I just stand there staring at the asphalt. They repaved that section of Route 9 back in October, and it already has potholes...

turns.doctor_question: Has this feeling of sadness and lack of interest been going on nearly every day for at least two weeks?
turns.patient_response:
Two weeks? Oh, no, it's been so much longer than that. This heavy feeling... the guilt, the just having no energy and not even wanting to eat... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. I remember because it started right around the time the grocery store down the street changed their layout. They moved the bakery section to the front, right by the sliding doors. I used to go in just to smell the bread. My grandmother used to bake bread every Sunday. Sourdough, mostly. She kept her starter in this old glass jar on top of the fridge. She said the warmth from the fridge helped it grow. She had that fridge for like twenty years, one of those almond-colored ones from the eighties. It had a handle that you had to pull really hard to open, and the seal was kind of sticky. We put all my report cards on it with these little magnetic alphabet letters. I think I lost the letter 'J' somewhere under the stove... 

But yeah, it's been over a year. A year and two months of feeling like this every single day.
